shifts.summary: The overall paper was seen as Moderate to Difficult by most reports. Reasoning was the easiest section, with candidates attempting 18–23 questions well. General Awareness and Quantitative Aptitude were the tougher sections, with good attempts around 14–18 and 13–20 respectively. English showed mixed difficulty, but most candidates managed 19–22 questions.

sections.notes: Questions were generally easy, some took extra time.

sections.notes: Questions varied across history, geography and current affairs; some were indirect.

observations: Sectional timing introduced caused extra pressure and time loss.
Quantitative Aptitude and General Awareness were reported as the toughest sections.
Reasoning was generally easier with most candidates attempting most questions well.
English questions were mixed; some were simple passages while others were lengthy and indirect.
disagreements: Reasoning difficulty reported as Easy, Moderate and Easy to Moderate.
General Awareness difficulty ranged from Moderate to Hard/Difficult.
Quant difficulty described as Difficult, Hard or Moderate to Difficult.
English difficulty varied between Easy, Easy to Moderate and Moderate/Hard for beginners.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 28 October 2026 was conducted in three shifts. Shift 1 has a reported analysis, while shift 2 has a partial review that requires further corroboration, and shift 3 is still pending with no usable analysis published yet. The difficulty levels are described as moderate to difficult overall, with section‑wise performance varying across shifts. All figures presented are unofficial and the SSC normalises scores across shifts.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty level was reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 28 October 2026?
faqs.a: Both shift 1 and shift 2 were described as moderate to difficult overall, based on the candidate reports available for 28 October 2026.

faqs.q: How did candidates perform in the Reasoning section on 28 October 2026 across the reported shifts?
faqs.a: In shift 1, candidates attempted 18–23 Reasoning questions well; in shift 2, the range was about 18–20 good attempts. No data is available yet for shift 3.

faqs.q: What does the partial analysis for shift 2 on 28 October 2026 indicate about its reliability?
faqs.a: The partial status means that a limited review of shift 2 has been published, but the findings need additional corroboration before they can be considered fully reliable.

faqs.q: Why is there no usable analysis for shift 3 on 28 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 3 is marked as pending, indicating that sufficient candidate evidence has not yet been gathered to produce a usable analysis.

faqs.q: Are the good‑attempt figures for the sections on 28 October 2026 official?
faqs.a: No. The good‑attempt numbers presented for the sections are unofficial estimates and should be treated as indicative rather than official statistics.
